column1: #mapping_set_title: CALM to NIST OSCAL class mappings

#mapping_set_description: "Schema-level mappings between the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (CALM 1.2) and NIST OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language). CALM's control framework is the primary interoperability target: Control and ControlRequirement map to OSCAL Control; ControlDetail maps to the implemented-requirement layer; EvidenceDocument maps to AssessmentResults. The Architecture document root relates to the OSCAL System Security Plan container."

column7: CALM Control is a named, domain-scoped control requirement attached to a node or relationship; OSCAL Control is the canonical structured representation of a security control in a catalog or profile.
CALM ControlRequirement defines a domain control schema (id, name, description); OSCAL Control captures the same specification with richer prose and parameter binding.

CALM ControlDetail pairs a requirement-url with an inline or referenced config; OSCAL SspImplementedRequirement pairs a control reference with an implementation statement - both record how a control is satisfied.
CALM EvidenceDocument links evidence paths to a control config URL; OSCAL AssessmentResults is the structured container for evidence collected during an assessment.
A CALM Architecture document describes a software system's structure including controls; an OSCAL System Security Plan describes the same system from a security authorisation perspective.
A CALM Node represents a logical or physical architecture element; an OSCAL SSP inventory item catalogues the components of an information system - both enumerate system elements.

A CALM Flow traces business transactions across relationships; OSCAL SspControlImplementation groups the implemented control statements - related as both describe cross-cutting behaviour of the system.
A CALM Timeline records architecture snapshots over time; OSCAL AssessmentResultsDocument records security posture at a point in time - both capture temporal views of a system.
